summary: This standards-track memo defines a DHCPv6 option for giving a client a list of SNTP server addresses. This lets a client learn which time servers to use as part of its automatic configuration.

eli5.summary: When a computer joins a network, it can be told where to ask for the correct time. This option carries that information.

questions: how does dhcpv6 provide time servers
what is the dhcpv6 sntp option
how does dhcpv6 provide sntp servers
subtitle: A DHCPv6 option that hands a client a list of IPv6 addresses of SNTP time servers.

tldr.problem: A DHCPv6 client has no built-in way to learn which SNTP servers it can use to set its clock.
tldr.mechanism: A new option, OPTION_SNTP_SERVERS (code 31), carries one or more 16-byte IPv6 server addresses in an ordered list.
tldr.outcome: Clients can learn time servers from DHCPv6, but a rogue DHCPv6 server could point them at a bad one, so authenticated DHCPv6 is advised.

today: RFC 4075 is a Proposed Standard and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: What the Option Is For
sections.content:
RFC 4075 defines the SNTP servers option for DHCPv6. It provides a list of one or more IPv6 addresses of SNTP servers available to the client, which uses them to synchronize its system time to that of the standard time servers.

It covers only SNTP servers reachable over IPv6. The DHCP option for IPv4 SNTP servers is in RFC 2132, and mechanisms for dual-stack applications are not specified.
sections.eli5: It is a note on the network's welcome sheet that says 'ask these clocks for the right time'.

sections.title: Option Format
sections.content:
The option has an option-code of OPTION_SNTP_SERVERS (31), an option-len and then one 128-bit IPv6 address per server. option-len is the length of the server fields in octets and must be a multiple of 16.

Clients MUST treat the list as ordered, and the server MAY list servers in decreasing order of preference.
sections.eli5: The option is a list of addresses, each the same size, and the first ones are the favourites.

sections.title: Where the Option May Appear
sections.content:
The option MUST NOT appear in messages other than Solicit, Advertise, Request, Renew, Rebind, Information-Request and Reply; a receiver SHOULD ignore it elsewhere.

Its option number MAY appear in the Option Request Option in Solicit, Request, Renew, Rebind, Information-Request and Reconfigure messages. A receiver SHOULD ignore it in other messages.
sections.eli5: There is a short list of DHCPv6 messages where this note is allowed. Anywhere else, it is ignored.

sections.title: Rogue Servers and Time
sections.content:
An intruder DHCPv6 server could use this option to make clients contact a rogue SNTP server, causing invalid time synchronization. Time accuracy can be crucial to security algorithms: expired certificates may gain a new life, and clients become vulnerable to replay attacks in protocols that use time stamps.

To avoid this, the DHCPv6 client SHOULD use authenticated DHCPv6. IANA assigned option code 31 to OPTION_SNTP_SERVERS.
sections.eli5: If a trickster hands out wrong clocks, your computer could believe old things are still fresh, so check who is giving the list.

fields.name: option-len
fields.desc: Length of the server fields in octets; a multiple of 16.
